bodyMarkdown:
Where the Cumberland crosses the hard Lower Pennsylvanian Rockcastle conglomerate, softer rock below erodes faster and keeps a ~68-foot, 125-foot-wide drop—the “Niagara of the South.” The falls likely began near the Pottsville Escarpment by Burnside and retreated about 45 miles upstream, cutting the gorge.

On clear full-moon nights the mist throws a moonbow, the only place in the Western Hemisphere where moonbows are known to appear with regularity. T. Coleman du Pont offered to buy the falls and surrounding land for a state park but died first; his widow completed the purchase in 1930, the family gave it to Kentucky, and the park was dedicated on August 21, 1931.
Source: [Cumberland Falls State Resort Park history (Kentucky State Parks, archived)](https://web.archive.org/web/20150604135131/http://parks.ky.gov/parks/resortparks/cumberland-falls/history.aspx)
